value: hydrogen direct reduction (H-DR) steelmaking: an electrolyser supplies H2 to a Midrex-type reduction shaft operating at 800 degC; the DRI is compacted to hot-briquetted iron (HBI) and melted to liquid steel in an EAF. Surplus H2 is recycled and a condenser recovers heat to pre-heat the H2 feed. All process heat is electric. Model plant, not an operating one; system boundary excludes pelletising, casting and rolling

note: HYBRIT, GrInHy and H2FUTURE were started 2016-2017; the only commercial hydrogen direct reduction was the Circored fluidised-bed plant in Trinidad, with H2 from steam reforming. Components (shaft, EAF, electrolyser) are each commercial.

per tonne of LIQUID STEEL, base case: 100% HBI charge, hydrogen feed ratio lambda = 1.5, 94% metallisation, hot HBI charged to the EAF, electrolyser 72% LHV. Two thirds of it is the electrolyser (Fig. 2). Excludes pelletising and rolling (a further 2.2 GJ/t fuel and 140 kWh/t electricity on any route, per Worrell et al. 2008). Comparator given: BF/BOF within comparable boundaries 13.3 GJ/t (3.68 MWh/t), from Otto et al. 2017. Sensitivities: +41.0 kWh/tLS per unit increase in lambda; +159 kWh/tLS if the HBI is charged cold. With a 50% scrap charge the electrolyser energy halves (Fig. 2, not tabulated).

COST BASIS: total-plant. Per tonne of annual liquid-steel capacity: electrolyser 160 + shaft 230 + EAF 184.
